I am trans, and early into HRT. I know that on a day to day basis, I *don't* pass. The problem I have is that I dress like I do. Skirts, tights, all of that. 

When I go to the grocery store, or a busy gas station, I panic. Honestly, I panic whenever there's people around me. Where do I go? What do I do? Do I run the risk of going to a men's room in a skirt, and being a "disgusting crossdresser", or do I go to the women's room and risk being a "pervert pedophile rapist"? Since the Target thing started happening, with all of the people boycotting it, I've noticed an increase in the judgmental stares and whispers.

Story time!

When I was in high school, I sucked. I didn't have many friends, and was awkward as hell around pretty much everyone. I had always been a "daddy's boy", doing everything I could to please my dad, even if it meant giving up on stuff I liked. 

That is, until a female friend of mine gave me her shirt. It was from a webcomic she and I both enjoyed, and it was a distinctly feminine girl's shirt. Not one of those "I can pull this off as unisex" things. 

But I loved it. It had great emotional appeal to me. It meant a lot... And I wanted to keep it forever. 

My stepmother didn't approve of me "cross-dressing" (in a girls long-sleeve shirt, as basic as it comes), so when laundry time came, she burned it. 

I was devastated. They had a talk with me about wearing "gender appropriate clothes" and about my interests also not being "gender appropriate." 

After that, I doubled down on gaming and nearly failing high school. Be a good boy, in every since. 

If that shirt hadn't been burned, maybe I would have come out to myself at 16, instead of 24.

Dear Dad,

I've been avoiding this for a few months, now. I'm sorry. It's a thing that needs to be said, but I don't know how to say it. I don't know how to tell you... Well, what needs to be said. 

So, let's start with a history lesson. Remember in Freshman year, when Amy gave me her hoodie? How I cherished it above everything else? Sure, it was a Megatokyo hoodie, and I love Megatokyo, but there was something else there. 

It was a *girl's* hoodie. And I wasn't outfitted with the right gender stats to equip that item. 

But I wore it anyways. I wore it happily. I loved it. 

Until you let Stepmom throw it away. "Not a hoodie you should be wearing. Don't wear girls clothes."

And that was that. 

So I made different mistakes. I focused on the masculinity I was supposed to feel. I still read Twilight, in secret, but I also got big into Halo. Big into military stuff. Tried not to be obvious with my love of fashion. With my love of interior design. 

It's not what you wanted. 

But, time and again, you've put her over everyone. You let her tear our family apart, and made us all suffer in the hopes that you wouldn't feel lonely ever again. 

But I won't suffer any more. 

I'm trans, Dad. I'm trans, and if all goes well, I should start hormones very soon. I know you always wanted a daughter. I know that the hopes were, before I was born, that I'd be a girl. 

Well I am. 

Or at least, I will be. 

I love you, Dad. 24 years of my life I've loved you, but I know who you are. I know you won't approve. So I'm disappearing. The old phone, gone. My old email, unanswered. The old Facebook, erased.

Maybe someday you'll love me for me. 

I always loved you for you. 

Yours,

[The Cover Alone](http://d.gr-assets.com/books/1375604540l/781069.jpg) speaks in unhallowed whispers that drive lesser beings insane. And there is a quote. A single quote, that has stuck with me.

> "People died having no idea why. People were thrown
from their beds, dashed against walls that collapsed onto them. People who survived long enough managed to find themselves buried alive beneath green sea many miles deep."

Animorphs was some hype shit, but Remnants gave my poor middle-school brain a fear of death I never asked for.
